summary: Forest Service lookout in Phelps County: 1937-41 CCC-era records, a survey note that it blew down, and a 2023 article describing a tower on the trail. Status disputed.

facts.status_note: One lookout site lists it as removed. A January 2023 article describes a fire tower on the trail, surrounded by barbed wire, and says climbing is not allowed.

corrections.why: A January 2023 article describes a fire tower on the Piney Lookout Tower Trail, surrounded by barbed wire, but places the trail on the west side of Table Rock Lake, which does not match the survey's Phelps County location. The Central US Lookouts page marks the lookout removed and the 1947 survey note says it blew down. The article alone does not establish that a tower stands at the surveyed site. A site check or a recent photo is needed before the record changes.

sources.title: You Can Hike to This Missouri Fire Tower, But Don't Climb It

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on status. The Central US page marks the lookout Removed and its 1947 survey note says the tower blew down and was to be rebuilt on the same foundation. A January 2023 article (101 The Eagle, a secondary and fairly casual source) describes a fire tower on the trail, surrounded by barbed wire. The article places the trail on the west side of Table Rock Lake, which does not match the Phelps County location of the survey, so its geography is unreliable. Whether the 2023 tower is the CCC-era structure or a rebuild is unknown. The 1937 plan was for a temporary crow's nest; the sources do not say whether it became the later tower. The blow-down note is undated. No build date, height or design is given in any source; the record has no height, and none is added. Worth a site visit or a recent photo, and a check against Forest Service records for the Piney site.
